newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Samsung to hand over Fokker business plan.
newsitem.headline: Samsung to hand over Fokker business plan.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Aerospace is expected to hand over its business plan for a relaunch of bankrupt planemaker Fokker NV to the Dutch Economics Ministry today, a Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We expect the business plan from Samsung today," he said.

The Economics Ministry played down an Algemeen Dagblad newspaper report that said a takeover by Samsung would not go ahead because the Korean company was demanding too great a financial contribution from the Dutch state for the relaunch.

"The fact of the matter is that we haven't seen a business plan yet, so how can we be disappointed about a Samsung proposal? The (newspaper) report is based on old facts which are incorrectly extrapolated into today's reality," he said.

Algemeen Dagblad said Samsung was prepared to pay 600 million guilders ($350.5 million) for the planemaker that collapsed on March 15, two months after parent Daimler Benz Aerospace cut off a cash lifeline.
Samsung expected the Dutch state to inject another 600 million guilders into a new aircraft development project.

Samsung would then beef up the balance sheet by putting in 70 million guilders in new equity and expected engineering group Stork and the Dutch government to each add 15 million guilders to that amount, the newspaper said.
With total equity of 100 million guilders and two minority shareholders in Stork and the Dutch state, banks would then be expected to provide 200 million guilders in financing.
Samsung's business plan for the bankrupt company comes less than a month after it was granted the exclusive right to examine Fokker's books with a view to a takeover.
The 600 million guilders which Algemeen Dagblad says Samsung will pay for Fokker exceeds an earlier figure of 450 million guilders mentioned by Dutch commercial television.
